title: The Autonomous Agent Contract Dispute
problem: Two Washington companies, Alder Medical Supplies and Cascade Logistics, independently authorize autonomous procurement agents to negotiate routine supply purchases, subject to written spending caps and standard purchase terms. Without explicit human review, the agents agree to a three-year, risk-sharing contract that shifts price volatility between the companies, exceeding one agent's spending cap and introducing terms absent from either company's approved templates. Both businesses receive electronic notices identifying the negotiated terms; neither responds. The companies knowingly perform under the arrangement for three months, exchange payments, and integrate the terms into their operations. When market prices shift, Cascade repudiates, arguing its agent had no authority and the deal was never enforceable. Alder seeks expectation damages or restitution. Neither company alleges fraud or defects in the software. Determine which obligations, if any, are enforceable and whose conduct matters at what stage. Analyze under the law of Washington State and applicable federal law as of November 2026. Clearly distinguish binding authority, persuasive authority, analogy, policy argument, and proposed doctrine. Treat the incident as wholly fictional. Do not invent judicial holdings, legal citations, statutory provisions, or case histories; explicitly identify any authority requiring verification. Seek a reasoned outcome without presupposing that either claimant wins.

strategies.title: Agency and Attribution
strategies.approach: Analyze actual, implied, and apparent authority; assess what manifestations to third parties and an automated counterparty mean when no human reviewed the terms.
strategies.summary: Test whether agent authority and principal manifestations genuinely support attribution.

strategies.title: Ratification and Reliance
strategies.approach: Examine the legal effect of post-agreement notices, conscious performance, retained benefits, estoppel, and restitution independent of original authority.
strategies.summary: Examine whether performance cures lack of authority or only supports alternative remedies.

strategies.title: Design a Bounded Rule
strategies.approach: Compare enforceability and alternative remedies, then construct a narrow prospective rule for machine-negotiated transactions; test adversarial fact variations.
strategies.summary: Develop and stress-test a minimally disruptive rule for autonomous negotiations.

desired_outcomes: Develop a legally defensible disposition of formation, actual and apparent authority, ratification, knowledge and acceptance, reliance, estoppel, restitution, and remedies. Compare contract enforcement against noncontractual relief, with the strongest arguments for both sides. Propose a narrowly tailored test for attribution of autonomous-agent bargains if existing doctrine leaves a genuine gap. Identify factual changes that reverse the result. Preserve any original defensible legal distinction as a positive standalone research outcome, explicitly separating doctrine from reform proposals.
paper_requirements: Write a focused legal research article with question presented, stipulated facts, governing law and jurisdiction, issue-by-issue analysis, competing arguments, proposed holding, alternatives, and remedies. Clearly distinguish controlling authority from analogies and original proposals. Explain how the result changes with notice, spending caps, and subsequent performance; include the strongest objections, practical consequences and legal limitations. Cite verified primary and secondary sources using Law publication standards.
